result.title: Change the Base, Change the Game: Rethinking Pan-sharpening
result.comment: The first two authors contributed equally to this work (equal contribution). Please visit our project page at this https://kaist-viclab.github.io/PanBase_site/
result.summary: Many pan-sharpening (PS) networks reconstruct high-resolution multispectral (HRMS) images by adding learned residuals to 4$\times$-interpolated low-resolution multispectral (LRMS) inputs, incorporating panchromatic (PAN) detail only through these residual corrections. This raises a simple question: Why start with a blurry base when sharp spatial detail is already available? We propose PanBase, a sharper multispectral starting point designed for more effective residual learning. Guided by physical sensor characteristics, PanBase combines PAN spatial detail with LRMS spectral information while enforcing consistency with the LRMS observations under sensor-specific blur. We construct this base without neural network training, estimating only nine coefficients per spectral band through closed-form calibration. Our PanBase can be easily integrated into existing backbones with a global residual skip through two simple changes: (i) replacing the skip base with PanBase and (ii) concatenating it as an additional input. Using each backbone's original training recipe and matched training budgets, PanBase improves most reduced- and full-resolution metrics on WorldView-3, QuickBird, and GaoFen-2, while achieving 4.4$\times$ faster training convergence on average. In zero-shot evaluation on WorldView-2, standalone PanBase achieves competitive reconstruction without target-sensor fitting or neural refinement.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文面向遥感全色锐化，提出基于传感器物理特性的 PanBase 初始基底，通过闭式标定少量系数并与 PAN 细节融合，替代插值 LRMS 作为残差学习的起点，从而提升重建指标并加快收敛。
AI.relevance_reason: 全色锐化属于图像融合与复原任务，其“更换残差基底”仅涉及输入构造与训练效率，未触及视觉推理中的内部状态表示、证据获取、动态计算或停止决策，缺少可供核查的 LVR 借鉴线索。
